elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 9.1 only requires performance "in accordance with the Performance Standards and, where there are no Performance Standards, in a commercially reasonable manner and with no other or higher degree of care"; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard formulation was added.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: New 16.1.G: "M&I warrants that, for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the software used to provide the Services will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: New 16.1.G sets the period at "ninety (90) days following delivery", i.e. the fallback duration, not 12 months.
Section 9.1 imposes a continuing, term-long obligation to perform the Services to the Performance Standards, a duration exceeding 90 days (though framed as a covenant rather than a warranty).

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: New 16.1.G: "M&I shall repair or replace the non-conforming software..."
New 16.1.G: "...or refund the fees paid for the affected Services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rendered language reproduces only 16.1.A, B, F and new G; subsections C–E of Section 16.1 are not before us, so a compliance-with-laws warranty may or may not exist. Nothing in the redline adds one.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in the rendered text (16.1.A, B, F, G); unquoted subsections C–E cannot be assessed. The redline adds none.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: New 16.1.G expressly warrants the software used to provide the Services will "conform in all material respects to its documentation" for "ninety (90) days following delivery" — a true software-to-documentation warranty, not merely report conformity with the User Manuals under 16.1.B.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Section 9.1 obligates M&I throughout the Term to "perform the Services in accordance with the Performance Standards and, where there are no Performance Standards, in a commercially reasonable manner" — an operative, continuing services performance standard well beyond 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: New 16.1.G: "For breach of this warranty, M&I shall repair or replace the non-conforming software..."
New 16.1.G alternative remedy: "...or refund the fees paid for the affected Services."

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: new 16.1.G supplies the 90-day software-to-documentation warranty plus repair/replacement and refund remedies, and Section 9.1's term-long Services performance obligation exceeds the 30-day services duration.

Preferred is not reached: the software period remains 90 days rather than 12 months, no "professional and workmanlike" services standard was added (9.1 caps the standard at "commercially reasonable" with "no other or higher degree of care"), and compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties are not shown in the rendered text. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to extend G to twelve (12) months, restate 9.1 or add a subsection warranting professional and workmanlike performance consistent with industry standards, and add express compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: a single new subsection G was inserted with no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or extra damages language, and no duplication of the existing 16.1.A/B warranties; the finding correctly relies on the existing carve-out rather than editing 16.1.F.

Intent preserved: 16.1.F's disclaimer opens "EXCEPT AS SPECIFICALLY SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION 16.1", so G is automatically carved out, and 9.1's "no other or higher degree of care" is subject to "Except as otherwise specified in this Agreement", so no retained sentence contradicts G.

Optional tightening (not a defect): G refers to lowercase "its documentation" while the Agreement elsewhere uses the defined "User Manuals"; anchoring G to the User Manuals and customer bulletins would remove any argument about which documents govern conformance.
